adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:75 — An _en file maps to itself as its "English" source, so every anchor in English (any href including javascript:, any on* attribute) is accepted by the self-match, and translations need only copy the text exactly; anchor attributes are never sanitized anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: In verifySafeHtml(), the “English source” file path is derived by regex-replacing the locale suffix with “_en.properties”. If the current file is already an _en.properties file under “resources” (not “resources-community”), englishFile resolves to the same file, so bundleEnglish == bundle. Then santizeAnchors() compares anchor tags in value vs. englishValue and, on exact match, removes the anchor tags from value before OWASP sanitization. Because <a> is not allowed by POLICY_SOME_HTML and anchors are stripped prior to policy.sanitize(), anchor attributes (e.g., href="javascript:...", on* handlers) are never validated/sanitized; they are implicitly trusted if they appear in the English file (self-match case) and copied verbatim in translations (exact-match case).

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:126 — For linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit* and error-invalid-multivalued-size the whole `{N,choice,...}` block is replaced with "..." before sanitizing, so HTML inside a choice arm (e.g. `{0,choice,0#|1#x}`) gets past the gate.

adjudication.rationale: In `normalizeValue()`, for keys starting with `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit` or equal to `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, the code does `value = value.replaceAll("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", "...");` before running OWASP sanitization/comparison. This strips the entire `{N,choice,...}` block from the string being checked, so any HTML inside a choice arm would be removed and therefore not detected/flagged by `verifySafeHtml()`, creating a false-negative in the verifier (i.e., malicious HTML could bypass this check).

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:79 — A missing English counterpart (e.g. an _en file under resources-community, or a translation whose English source is in another module) throws an unchecked RuntimeException instead of adding a message or throwing MojoExecutionException, so the build aborts on the first such file and the remaining files are never reported.

adjudication.rationale: In `verifySafeHtml()`, the code unconditionally constructs an `englishFile` path and then loads it via `new FileInputStream(englishFile)`. If that file does not exist or can’t be read, the `catch (IOException e)` block throws a new unchecked `RuntimeException` (not a `MojoExecutionException` and not adding to `messages`). This will abort execution on the first missing/invalid English counterpart and prevent reporting remaining issues, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:75 — The locale-suffix regex allows only letters, `-` and `_`, so a file with no suffix or with a digit locale (e.g. messages.properties, messages_es_419.properties) maps to itself, and the translation is then checked only against itself.

adjudication.rationale: In verifySafeHtml(), the English reference path is derived via `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. This pattern does not match digit-containing locale suffixes like `_es_419.properties` (because `419` contains digits), and it also won’t match files with no locale suffix (e.g. `messages.properties`). In those cases, `englishFile` remains the same locale file name, so the “English” bundle can end up being the same locale (or a non-existent file), causing the translation to be compared against itself and/or throwing when the expected English file isn’t found. This undermines the intended safety check that translations only allow HTML if the English source contains it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:91 — Any English tag at all, including a lone anchor, makes containsHtml true, so the translation may add any of br/p/strong/b even when the English uses none of them; the allow-list is not per-tag.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `containsHtml(englishValue)` returns true for any HTML tag via `HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, including a lone `<a ...>` in the English string. That boolean gates policy selection: `PolicyFactory policy = containsHtml(englishValue) ? POLICY_SOME_HTML : POLICY_NO_HTML;`, and `POLICY_SOME_HTML` allows `br`, `p`, `strong`, `b`. Since anchors are handled separately in `santizeAnchors(...)` and are not part of the OWASP allowlist, an English string that only contains `<a>` will still flip to `POLICY_SOME_HTML`, letting translations introduce `br/p/strong/b` even if the source didn’t use them. This is a real, diff-grounded permissiveness/design concern, but not a clearly verifiable defect given the in-code comment (“Only if the English source string contains HTML we also allow HTML in the translation”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:153 — Anchor matching accepts any in-order subset of the English anchors, so a translation that keeps `` but drops `` passes and ships an unclosed link.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(...)`, the loop only iterates over anchor tags found in the translation (`matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)`) and merely checks each one against the next anchor tag in the English source (`englishMatcher.find()`). It never verifies that the translation contains a complete/paired set of anchor tags (e.g., both `` and ``), nor that all required English anchors are present. Therefore a translation can include only the opening `` (dropping ``), match the first English `` and pass validation, allowing malformed/unclosed link markup to ship.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:157 — The "Didn't find anchor tag" message leaves out the key and the file, and the `break` stops at the first mismatch, so the report does not say where the problem is.

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors(...)`, on mismatch it reports only `"Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string"` and does not include `key` or `file`, unlike the other error messages in `verifySafeHtml()` which include both. Also, the `break;` immediately stops after the first mismatch, so additional mismatching `<a>` tags in the same value would not be reported. This is a concrete, diff-grounded diagnosability/reporting issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:133 — The RTL-style exemption applies to any file whose absolute path contains "email" (including parent directories such as a checkout folder), not just email themes.

adjudication.rationale: In `normalizeValue`, the RTL-style stripping is gated by `if (file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email"))`, which will match any absolute path segment containing the substring "email" (not just the intended email theme directory). This can incorrectly strip ` style="direction: rtl;"` from non-email message files when the checkout path or parent directories include "email", causing the HTML verifier to produce false negatives. This behavior is directly introduced by the added `verifySafeHtml()` logic.

adjudication.rationale: In both JS app bundles (js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties and js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties) the key `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from i18next-style `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` placeholders to MessageFormat-style `{0}` plus `{2,choice,...}`. adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:102 — Independent prefix/suffix trim loops can overlap (e.g. value `xy` vs sanitized `xy` gives start=2, end=8), making `substring(start, length-end)` throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and abort the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the diff-reporting logic computes `start` from the common prefix and `end` from the common suffix independently, then does `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` with no guard that `start <= length - end`. These loops can overlap when the sanitizer removes a middle portion, making `sanitized.length() - end` (or `value.length() - end`) less than `start`, which will throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` and abort verification instead of adding the intended message. The example in the finding (value contains an extra `` so suffix `y` matches almost entirely) is consistent with this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:75 — englishFile regex matches the leftmost `_` in the file name and rejects digits, so `foo_bar_de.properties` maps to `foo_en.properties` and a name with no match (e.g. `messages_es_419`) compares against itself, which silently skips the translation check

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English reference path is derived via `file.getAbsolutePath()...replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. This regex can start matching at the *first* underscore in the filename because `[a-zA-Z-_]*` is greedy and allows underscores, so a name like `foo_bar_de.properties` would match `_bar_de.properties` and become `foo_en.properties` (dropping `bar`). Also, because the character class excludes digits, a locale suffix containing digits (e.g. `_es_419.properties`) would not match at all, leaving `englishFile` unchanged (or only “resources-community” swapped), so the “English” bundle may end up being the same non-English file or an incorrect path. Both are correctness defects in the new translation/HTML policy comparison logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:79 — A missing or unreadable English counterpart throws a raw RuntimeException that escapes verify()'s MojoExecutionException contract instead of producing a proper build error or message

adjudication.rationale: In `verify()`, only `IOException` from `Files.readString(...)` is converted to `MojoExecutionException`, but the newly added `verifySafeHtml()` reads both the current file and an inferred English file and on `IOException` throws a raw `RuntimeException` (two `catch (IOException e) { throw new RuntimeException(...) }` blocks). If the English counterpart path is missing/unreadable (or the file itself can’t be read via `FileInputStream`), this `RuntimeException` will escape `verify()` without being wrapped as a `MojoExecutionException`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:154 — santizeAnchors pairs anchors strictly by position, so a translation that reorders the same anchors is falsely reported

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), anchor tags in the translation are validated by iterating matcher.find() and advancing englishMatcher.find() in lockstep, requiring exact positional order and exact string equality of each matched or . The method comment says it should "Allow only those anchor tags from the source key to also appear in the target key" (presence-based), but the implementation is order-based; if a translation contains the same anchor tags but reordered, the first mismatch will trigger "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" even though the tags exist in the source.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:157 — The "Didn't find anchor tag" message leaves out the key and the file (unlike the Illegal HTML message), so there is no way to trace the failure to its source across many files

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), the failure path logs `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")` without including either the `key` parameter or the current `file`. In contrast, the illegal-HTML path includes both key and file in the message (`"Illegal HTML in key " + key + " for file " + file + ...`). Given this verifier runs across many message files, lacking key/file context is a concrete, diff-grounded diagnosability problem (but not a functional defect in verification logic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:118 — Hardcoded key-specific exemptions (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) embed knowledge of specific theme messages in a generic verifier instead of a configurable allowlist.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `normalizeValue(...)` in `VerifyMessageProperties` with explicit, hardcoded exceptions for specific message keys (`templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, `error-invalid-multivalued-size`). This couples a supposedly generic theme verifier to particular theme message semantics instead of using a configurable/central allowlist or policy, which is a maintainability/architecture concern introduced by this change, not a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:74 — English-source path derived via string substitution of "resources-community" and a locale-suffix regex couples the verifier to the repo's directory layout and naming, and fails with a RuntimeException if no matching _en file exists.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `verifySafeHtml()` which derives the English properties path via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` and then unconditionally tries to open it. If that computed `_en` file does not exist (or path differs from assumptions), the `FileInputStream` throws `IOException` which is converted into an unchecked `RuntimeException` (`throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e);`). This can hard-fail the verifier/build rather than reporting a message, and it is directly introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:132 — RTL-style exemption keyed on the absolute path containing "email" is a fragile layout coupling that matches any path segment (e.g. parent dirs) and is marked TODO.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:157 — "Didn't find anchor tag" message omits the key and file name, unlike the other messages, making failures hard to locate across many translation files.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:67 — File is read twice (Files.readString in verify() then FileInputStream here) and IOException is wrapped in RuntimeException rather than following the existing MojoExecutionException handling in verify().

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:92 — The raw pattern is sanitized before MessageFormat quote handling, so a translation like `<'img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` or `'<'script'>'...` gets lexed as text and passes, but after msg()/MessageFormat strips the quotes it renders as a real tag (XSS bypass of the verifier).

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added verifySafeHtml(), the sanitizer is applied directly to the raw .properties value (after normalizeValue/unescape) and there is no handling of MessageFormat’s apostrophe-quoting rules. That means a crafted translation like `<'img src=x onerror=...>` could be treated as non-HTML by the OWASP sanitizer (since `<` is followed by `'` so it won’t parse as a tag) and thus pass verification, while later MessageFormat-style processing (not accounted for here) can remove the apostrophe and yield a real `` tag. The diff shows the verifier explicitly accommodates MessageFormat choice patterns but does not account for quote handling, so this is a real gap in the verifier’s correctness/security check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:126 — The choice exemption `\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}` replaces the whole choice body with "..." before sanitizing, so any HTML inside it (e.g. `{0,choice,0#|1#x}`) in linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.* (email) or error-invalid-multivalued-size is never checked.

adjudication.rationale: In `normalizeValue`, for keys starting with `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit` or equal to `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, the code does `value = value.replaceAll("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", "...");` before sanitizing. This removes the entire `{...,choice,...}` segment from the string being checked, so any HTML embedded inside the choice options would be eliminated and never compared against the sanitizer output, effectively bypassing the new illegal-HTML verification for those keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:120 — The templateHelp exemption `CLAIM\.<[A-Z]*>` also removes things like `CLAIM.<SCRIPT>`, `CLAIM.<IFRAME>` or `CLAIM.<PLAINTEXT>` before sanitizing, and HTML tag names are case-insensitive, so it hides real tags; it should match only the literal `CLAIM.<NAME>`.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue(), for key "templateHelp" the exemption `value.replaceAll("CLAIM\\.<[A-Z]*>", "")` will strip any uppercase placeholder like `CLAIM.<SCRIPT>` or `CLAIM.<IFRAME>` before the sanitizer runs. That means a translation could include tag-like payloads wrapped in `CLAIM.<...>` and the verifier would not report it, undermining the new HTML-safety verification introduced in this diff. The finding is directly grounded in the added code at the cited line.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:74 — For `*_en.properties` files the derived English path is the file itself, so English sources are checked against themselves: any anchor (e.g. javascript: href or on* attributes) is auto-approved and any key with a tag unlocks POLICY_SOME_HTML.

adjudication.rationale: In `verifySafeHtml()`, the “English source” bundle path is derived via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. For files that are already `*_en.properties` under `resources` (no `resources-community` in the path), this resolves to the same file, so `englishValue` == `value`. As a result, `santizeAnchors()` will always treat any `` / `` in the English string as “present in original”, remove those anchor tags from `value`, and thus bypass the OWASP sanitizer check for anchor attributes/schemes (e.g., `javascript:` href or `on*` attributes) in English strings. Also, since `containsHtml(englishValue)` is then true for any tag present in the English string, the code selects `POLICY_SOME_HTML` based on that self-reference rather than an external baseline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:155 — Successful anchor-match/strip path (replaceFirst of matching and ) is never exercised; changedAnchor_de only hits the mismatch branch

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java:33 — Duplicate-keys assertion weakened from contains to hasItem although the fixture still yields exactly one message, so unexpected extra messages (e.g. spurious Illegal HTML from the new self-comparison) would go unnoticed

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java:50 — changedAnchor_de produces both 'Didn't find anchor tag' and 'Illegal HTML' messages but the test checks only one via hasItem and the anchor message carries no key/file, which is never asserted

adjudication.rationale: From the added logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, `changedAnchor_de.properties` will (1) trigger `santizeAnchors()` to add a message `"Didn't find anchor tag ..."` without including the key/file, and then (2) still run OWASP sanitization where `<a ...>` is not allowed by `POLICY_SOME_HTML` (only `br,p,strong,b`), causing an additional `"Illegal HTML in key ... for file ..."` message. The test `verifyNoChangedAnchors()` asserts only that *some* item contains `"Didn't find anchor tag"` (via `hasItem`), and does not assert the presence/absence or formatting/context (key/file) of either message. adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:74 — English-file path derivation (resources-community -> resources, _zh_CN/_de -> _en regex) is untested; all fixtures sit in one directory with no resources-community or multi-segment locale case

adjudication.rationale: VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml() derives the English bundle path by string-rewriting the current file path: `replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` and `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`, then opens that file. The added tests only use fixtures under `misc/theme-verifier/src/test/resources/` (no `resources-community` segment in the path) and only cover a single-segment locale (`_de`), not multi-segment locales like `_zh_CN`. adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:79 — No test for a missing English counterpart file, which throws an unchecked RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException/message

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English bundle is loaded from a derived path (englishFile) and any IOException is converted to an unchecked RuntimeException (catch block when reading englishFile). This bypasses the method’s usual pattern of collecting validation messages and also bypasses MojoExecutionException handling in verify(). The added tests cover illegal HTML, no-HTML translations, and changed anchors, but none exercise the case where the derived English counterpart file is missing/unreadable, so this edge-case behavior isn’t tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:168 — No test for a key missing from the English bundle (falls back to "" and forces POLICY_NO_HTML)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new HTML-safety verification logic. In `getEnglishValue(...)`, a missing key in the English bundle is caught and returns `""` (see `catch (MissingResourceException ex) { englishValue = ""; }`). Then `containsHtml(englishValue)` will be false, causing `POLICY_NO_HTML` to be applied to the translated value (`PolicyFactory policy = containsHtml(englishValue) ? POLICY_SOME_HTML : POLICY_NO_HTML;`). The added tests cover illegal HTML tags, “no HTML allowed” when English has none, and changed anchors, but none covers the case where the key is missing from the English bundle and thus falls back to empty string / `POLICY_NO_HTML`. This is a specific uncovered edge-case introduced by the new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:117 — normalizeValue special cases (templateHelp CLAIM.<NAME>, optimizeLookupHelp <Extensions>, choice-format '<', email rtl style stripping via path contains("email")) have no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue()` with multiple key/path-specific branches (e.g., `templateHelp` stripping `CLAIM\.<[A-Z]*>`, `optimizeLookupHelp` stripping `<Extensions>`, replacing `{...,choice,...}` for keys including `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, and removing ` style="direction: rtl;"` when the file path contains `"email"`). The accompanying tests/fixtures added in this PR only cover duplicate key detection, illegal HTML tag detection, disallowing HTML when the English source has none, and changed anchor tags (`duplicateKeys_en.properties`, `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `noHtml_*.properties`, `changedAnchor_*.properties`). None of the fixtures reference `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, `error-invalid-multivalued-size` choice normalization, or the email RTL stripping branch, so those special cases are not exercised by tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:111 — Diff-trimming prefix/suffix logic is untested and can overlap (e.g. value "aa" vs sanitized "a" gives start=1,end=1) causing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException in sanitized.substring

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), when sanitized != value it computes `start` and `end` by stripping common prefix/suffix, then builds an error message using `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)`. There is no guard to ensure `start <= sanitized.length() - end` (or value’s). If sanitized is shorter but shares both a prefix and a suffix with value (e.g., value="aa", sanitized="a"), the loops can yield `start=1` and `end=1`, making `sanitized.length()-end` 0 and causing `sanitized.substring(1,0)` -> StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This is a real crash path in the new diff-trimming logic, and the added tests don’t cover this edge case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/test/resources/illegalHtmlTag_en.properties:17 — Illegal-tag fixture is an English file compared against itself with a malformed '</div' tag, so it does not cover a translated file carrying a disallowed tag that the English source lacks/has

adjudication.rationale: It’s true that `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties` will be compared against itself because `verifySafeHtml()` derives `englishFile` by rewriting the locale suffix to `_en.properties`, which for an `_en` fixture resolves to the same file. However, the finding’s implication that this leaves the “translated file contains disallowed HTML while English lacks it” case untested is contradicted by the diff: `verifyNoHtmlAllowed()` uses `noHtml_de.properties` vs `noHtml_en.properties` to cover exactly that scenario (translation has `<b>`, English has no HTML).
